geo.label: tariff reset / hold
parts: Macro Stance

The US picture is growth that slowed sharply at year-end, with inflation still above the 2% goal and a tariff regime that is still moving. GDP growth fell to a 1.4% rate in the fourth quarter [[n6592]], while January payrolls rose by 130,000 [[n6365]] and consumer prices were up 2.4% over the year to January [[n6488]]. Fed officials are leaning towards a pause: Waller said a pause may be appropriate if January's upside jobs surprise continues [[n6622]], and Goolsbee wants a hold on cuts because current inflation is 'not good enough' [[n7223]]. Stance: Mixed. The data supports waiting for the next print, but the tariff rules matter more for the next six months than the Fed's first move. Weekly jobless claims fell by the most since November to 206,000 [[n6528]], which supports the view that the labour market is stable rather than deteriorating.
Rates & Curve

The 2Y closed at 3.45% and the 10Y at 4.05% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-25), leaving the 10Y-2Y spread at 60 bps. Over 20 sessions the 10Y is down 19 bps and the 2Y is down 8 bps, which makes this a bull flattening (both down, 10Y down more), and the curve is moderately steep, approaching the long-run average. The 30Y closed at 4.70% and the 3M at 3.69%, and nothing in the card points to a long-end sell-off. Mortgage rates have followed yields lower, with the 30-year fixed at 5.76% in one Yahoo Finance headline [[n6682]] and the lowest since 2022 in a Bloomberg headline [[n6724]]. The S&P 500 closed at 6,946.13, 0.47% lower over 20 sessions, the Nasdaq 100 at 25,329.04 is 2.35% lower, the VIX is at 17.93 and the DXY at 97.70 is 1.54% higher (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). Treasury yields have reacted to the trade headlines: they fell as investors weighed the new tariffs [[n7117]] and edged higher after the State of the Union [[n7367]].
New / Most Important

The most important new fact is that the tariff regime was reset. The Supreme Court struck down the emergency tariffs and the administration moved to a new global tariff that starts at 10% [[n7313]], with Trump wanting it at 15% 'where appropriate' [[n0931]]. Refunds are a fiscal problem as well: Penn-Wharton estimates that over $175 billion of revenue is subject to refunds [[n7440]], and the State of the Union did not mention them [[n0942]]. Bond traders are betting that Fed cuts spill into 2027 [[n7350]], so the rate path and the tariff path are now linked through the deficit. The consumer is split. The Conference Board finds only Gen Z and millennials optimistic about the economy [[n6707]], and Goldman Sachs says American consumers are stuck with high prices even after the tariff ruling [[n6628]].
Playbook ✓

Mixed. Keep a benchmark US equity book but hedge the Nasdaq 100 for tariff headlines, since the index is 2.35% lower over 20 sessions. Hold duration rather than cash while the curve bull-flattens and the 10Y is 19 bps lower over 20 sessions. Trigger to add risk: a 2Y yield back above its 20-session reference of 3.53% would signal that the market has given up on near-term cuts, which is a reason to buy the banks. Trigger to cut risk: the VIX, up 9.66% over 20 sessions, extending its rise on tariff headlines. Nvidia's record quarter [[n5412]] supports semiconductors, but the broad index is not yet confirming the rally. The AI scare trade is a separate signal: one Business Insider headline says stocks are flashing a signal that the scare could lead to a sharper decline [[n7395]], which is why the Nasdaq hedge matters.

geo.label: hold / leadership transition
parts: Macro Stance

Europe is the strongest equity story on the card: the STOXX 600 is up 4.10% over 20 sessions, the CAC 40 up 6.10%, the FTSE 100 up 6.42% and the DAX up 1.42% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). European shares closed at a record on HSBC's boost and easing AI disruption fears [[n2288]], and the rally also reflected easing tariff fears [[n2294]]. Stance: Mixed. The euro is 2.02% lower over 20 sessions at 1.1775, and Europe's trade with the US is still hostage to Washington, with the European Parliament freezing the US trade deal [[n2851]]. Brussels remains fragmented on Russia: Hungary is blocking new EU sanctions over a pipeline dispute [[n2868]], and the EU has failed to pass new sanctions after Hungary objected [[n2866]].
Credit & Inflation

Euro-area inflation was 1.7% in January, Eurostat confirmed [[n2273]], and ECB Governing Council member Vujcic said the bank must not be complacent on inflation [[n2260]]. Panetta said Chinese imports helped drive a sharper-than-forecast drop in inflation [[n2124]], which leaves the disinflation debate open. Euro-zone businesses performed better than expected in February as manufacturing bounced back [[n2079]]. On credit, the ECB is stepping up scrutiny of European banks' AI exposure [[n2155]], and Bloomberg reports that souring bond deals threaten a Nordic credit boom [[n2521]].
New / Most Important

The ECB leadership is now in play. Economists expect Lagarde to exit early and hand the job to Knot [[n2261]], although Lagarde has said she expects to finish her term [[n2064]]. Bloomberg frames a March date set by the EU for the customs race as a prelude to the ECB tussle [[n2263]]. Germany's Merz used his first Beijing trip to warn of a trade imbalance with China [[n2276]], which adds a trade-policy overlay to the monetary one.
Playbook ✓

Mixed. Own the European index against the euro's 2.02% fall over 20 sessions, since a weaker euro helps exporters, but keep the autos underweight. Trigger to turn Bullish on cyclicals: the EU Parliament restarting its approval of the US trade deal and no new US tariff step. Trigger to turn Bearish: a US move to 15% that the EU answers with retaliation [[n2224]]. Keep the ECB succession on the watch list, because a change at the top changes the rate path in the second half of the year. The sanctions fights do not move the broad equity story, but they do matter for defence names.

geo.label: targeted support / property drag
parts: Macro Stance

China's growth story is a consumption rebound on a weak investment base. The Lunar New Year holiday produced record tourism spending of $116 billion [[n0890]], and the longest holiday lifted travel spending [[n0861]]; the consumer shows up in holiday data, not in property. Policy is on hold: the benchmark lending rate has been left unchanged for a ninth straight month [[n0740]], and Capital Economics says the investment-led growth era is ending [[n0649]]. Stance: Mixed. The consumption upside is real but not yet broad.
PMIs & Activity

The feed carries no fresh official China manufacturing PMI in the window. The latest China services PMI headline is S&P Global's China General Services PMI from 4 February [[n0468]], and that headline carries no figure, so none is quoted here. The activity read therefore rests on holiday and box-office data, and the Lunar New Year box office fell to a six-year low [[n0807]], which says the consumption recovery is uneven. Confirmation would come from the next manufacturing and services prints: a factory reading above 50 with services holding would move the stance to Bullish.
Credit Impulse

The feed has no fresh total social financing or new-yuan-loan print, so the credit impulse cannot be measured from headlines. The best proxy is policy: the lending benchmark has been unchanged for nine months [[n0740]], and CNBC's headline points to China's leverage rising ahead of the summit [[n0755]]. Rising leverage is not the same as a credit impulse, and it is not yet visible in property or household credit. Until a TSF print turns positive, we read credit as stable, not expanding.
Property

The mainland property bust has not turned. The Economist describes the 'rotten tail' of the bust [[n0773]], and commercial property is suffering with empty shops and falling rents in the retail slump [[n0770]]. Shanghai eased residency requirements for homebuyers to spark a recovery [[n0922]]. Hong Kong is the bright spot: home prices reached a 19-month high [[n0921]] and analysts forecast a rise of at least 10% in 2026 [[n0920]]. Hong Kong is not the mainland, so that recovery is a Hong Kong trade; mainland easing is incremental.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

Beijing is pushing back on Washington. China said it has met its US trade obligations and warned against more tariffs [[n0930]], and it is assessing the Supreme Court ruling, saying 'fighting is harmful' [[n0729]]. A US–China summit is expected in April [[n0851]], and Beijing's leverage in the talks rose after the tariff ruling [[n0755]]. The sharper edge is Japan: China put Japanese entities on a dual-use blacklist [[n3251]] and restricted exports to Japanese firms with military ties [[n0834]]. The IMF urged China to shift to consumption-led rebalancing and to curb industrial policy [[n0901]], the policy gap the market is watching.
Markets & Flows

The Shanghai Composite closed at 4,147.23, up 0.82% over 20 sessions, and the Hang Seng at 26,765.72, up 0.06% over the same period (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The US-listed proxies disagree. ASHR, the CSI 300 tracker, rose 2.37% to 34.57, while KWEB, the internet ETF, fell 10.19% to 32.24 and FXI fell 3.81% to 38.42 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The yuan is the strongest leg: USD/CNY closed at 6.8831, 1.03% lower over 20 sessions, with the currency near a three-year high [[n0874]] even as traders pile into bearish yuan bets to hedge downside [[n0881]]. Foreign investors are buying Hong Kong and mainland stocks [[n0854]].
New / Most Important

The most important new fact is yuan strength on a steadier US track. Asian currencies hit a 16-month high on the weak dollar and the yuan's gains [[n0802]], and Bloomberg's headline says China wins as Trump is forced to rejig tariffs [[n0779]]. A tariff ruling that lowered the US tariff wall eases the pressure on Chinese exporters. For investors the question is whether the yuan rally can hold through the April summit, and whether the Hang Seng can follow it.
Playbook ✓

Mixed. Prefer broad A-share and Hong Kong exposure over the internet names: ASHR is up over 20 sessions while KWEB is 10.19% lower. Trigger to turn Bullish: a tariff settlement or a new consumption support package before the April summit. Trigger to turn Bearish: a summit that stalls alongside a fresh escalation with Japan over export controls. ⚠ Divergence: the yuan is near a three-year high and holiday spending is at records, yet the China internet ETF has lost 10.19% over 20 sessions and the Hang Seng is almost flat.

geo.label: hawkish BOJ / reflation board
parts: Macro Stance

Japan's policy debate has moved onto the BOJ board. The government picked two academics seen as reflationists [[n3239]], and the market read the choice as dovish [[n3272]], but the most hawkish member says a rate hike is needed soon [[n3271]]. The BOJ chief flagged a March or April rate-hike chance in an interview [[n3274]]. Stance: Mixed. The policy path is split inside the board, and the yen is the pressure valve. The yen has lost purchasing power, with the currency at a 53-year low on that measure [[n3190]], which keeps political pressure on the currency. Takaichi's election sweep lifted the yen briefly, but the open question is whether the move lasts [[n3217]].
Activity & Currency

Japan's CPI cooled to its slowest pace in two years on distortions [[n6533]], but services inflation held steady with wage-driven price pressure [[n6693]], and factory activity expanded at the fastest pace in four years [[n2018]]. USD/JPY closed at 155.88, up 2.25% over 20 sessions, and the Nikkei 225 closed at 58,583.12, up 10.77% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The yen hit a two-week low after the pro-stimulus appointments [[n3278]], and a US Treasury yen rate check in January [[n3242]] shows the authorities are watching the currency. Currency officials have been visible: the US led January yen rate checks and eyed a joint intervention with Japan [[n3216]], and Japan's finance minister says Tokyo is in close dialogue with Washington on forex [[n3220]].
Playbook ✓

Mixed: own the Nikkei, which is at a record, but pair it with a yen hedge because the currency is the risk. Be careful with ultra-long JGBs, where reflationist picks have pushed long-term yields up [[n3287]]. Trigger to turn Bullish on the yen: a BOJ hike in March [[n3215]] endorsed by the board. Trigger to turn Bearish on the yen: a hold with a dovish board majority and USD/JPY moving through its 155.88 close.

geo.label: tightening bias / hot core
parts: Macro Stance

The RBA is leaning towards a hike. The governor says inflation is not taking off again [[n0256]], but hot inflation figures kept a hike on the table [[n0218]], and core inflation reached a 16-month high, raising bets on a May hike [[n6656]]. The March meeting is a live question [[n0249]]. Stance: Mixed, with a tightening bias: the domestic rate path is hawkish while the equity market is still rising. The RBA is also explaining itself. Its deputy told shoppers to vote with their feet when companies take advantage [[n0186]], while the governor said the bank is studying monthly inflation data for a possible new policy gauge [[n0197]]. The Financial Review headline sums up the mood: rate calls are getting tougher [[n0250]].
Demand & Financing

AUD/USD closed at 0.7061, up 0.93% over 20 sessions, and the ASX 200 at 9,128.30, up 2.18% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). Carry-trade demand is lifting the currency [[n0251]]. Lenders are passing the cycle on: Westpac and CBA raised fixed rates [[n0259]], and borrowing costs are now a live household issue. On the demand side, unemployment is at 4.1% [[n0140]] and firms are cutting jobs, with WiseTech planning 2,000 cuts [[n0263]] and CBA 300 [[n0200]]. WiseTech's shares still rose 7% on its half-year results [[n1812]]. Share prices have not yet reflected the hike. The ASX 200 is up 2.18% over 20 sessions, while banks are the first place a hike shows up in earnings, which makes them the test of the call.
Playbook ✓

Mixed. Hold the ASX 200 with a bias to exporters and banks, since bank margins benefit from a hike, and keep AUD exposure hedged against a March hold. Trigger to add: a March hike that is not followed by a pause. Trigger to cut: a core inflation print that falls back, which would take the May-hike bet off the table.

geo.label: easing bias / weak activity
parts: Monetary & Activity

The NBP has a difficult call. January inflation came in above forecasts [[n3562]] even though it fell [[n3563]], and economists are split on a March cut [[n3567]]. Activity is weak: employment fell surprisingly and wages grew at their slowest pace in five years [[n3613]], and industrial output disappointed [[n3603]]. The budget is leaking: revenues were nearly 30 billion lower [[n3832]] and below plan [[n3836]], and the Commission warns that debt will breach 100% of GDP by 2036 [[n3425]]. Banks are buying government bonds and the KNF is watching closely [[n3828]], while the regulator has signalled moving away from WIBOR [[n3956]]. Housing is turning too: Poland saw its first annual house-price fall since 2013 [[n3413]].

Companies

Orlen is the state champion pulling capital. It plans to inject 5.1 billion zloty into utility Energa [[n3428]] and wants Energa to run a share issue with pre-emptive rights [[n3912]]; a former CBA head joins the Orlen board [[n3923]], and Orlen's plan has debt rising [[n3637]]. KGHM has a new CEO [[n3863]] and reached a wage agreement with unions [[n3942]]. Chemical maker Azoty seeks an 83% debt writedown in its polymer restructuring [[n3397]], with Orlen involved in the takeover talks [[n3783]]. Orlen is also changing household bills: its entry into the gas market will change what households pay [[n3911]].
Security & New Development

Security policy is now a market story. Poland withdrew from the treaty banning anti-personnel mines and will use them to defend against Russia [[n3382]], and the PM says the border can be mined within 48 hours [[n3357]]. Poland, Germany, France, Italy and the UK will develop low-cost air-defence systems [[n3406]], and Poland ended the special status of Ukrainian refugees [[n3374]]. Defence is a budget line that will compete with the deficit.
Playbook ✓

Mixed: own the state-linked cash generators, KGHM and PKN Orlen, for the commodity and reflation tailwind, avoid domestic-demand names until wages and jobs turn, and treat zloty weakness as a reason to hold dollars. Trigger to turn Bullish on domestic names: a March NBP cut paired with a labour rebound. Trigger to turn Bearish: a further budget revenue shortfall. ⚠ Divergence: state-linked stocks rallied hard, with KGHM up 13.17% over five sessions, while the labour and industrial data disappointed [[n3613]] and the budget is short of revenue [[n3832]].

Aston Martin issued another profit warning [[n1639]], and German car exports to China fell by a third in 2025 [[n0822]]. Tesla's European problem keeps getting worse [[n5156]].
EPS Upside Watch

Stellantis's earnings preview asks whether it is deep value or deep trouble [[n1697]]. Volkswagen's push into robotaxis [[n5526]] is the growth argument the sector lacks. Mercedes, Nissan and Stellantis are investing in the UK self-driving startup Wayve [[n5158]], which keeps the autos story tied to autonomy.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The EU delayed a plan that could protect Europe's EVs from Chinese rivals [[n5522]], yet the tracker is up 2.48% over 20 sessions. The market is looking past the policy risk that is squeezing sector margins.
Narrative

Semis lead the AI hardware trade: SOXX is up 4.82% over 20 sessions at 368.00, SMH is up 4.64%, and TSMC is up 14.60% at 387.73 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). Nvidia's record quarter [[n5412]] and TSMC's 28% dividend increase on 38% revenue growth [[n5407]] anchor the narrative.
Reported

Nvidia's forecast points to accelerating growth as Vera Rubin starts reaching the market [[n5418]]. ASML's EUV light source is making a breakthrough [[n5069]], and the company says AI demand is its long-term growth driver [[n5443]].
EPS Upside Watch

Micron is up 330% in a year [[n5479]], and memory prices are still rising [[n5477]]. The next Micron print will show whether pricing carries into earnings, and ASML's systems sales have grown in double digits [[n5070]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

The memory boom is a cost for device makers. HP warned that the memory crunch will linger into next year and PC sales will slump [[n5109]], and the FT says PC and smartphone makers are left in the cold [[n5475]]. Semis gain from the cost that hurts their customers.

earnings_pattern.title: Earnings Pattern: beats are not enough, guidance and AI exposure decide the move
parts: Rewarded

Beats with a raised outlook were paid. HSBC's shares hit a record as the bank lifted its target [[n0943]], and Deere's guidance boost sent its stock up [[n1584]]. Circle surged after a beat, with USDC circulation up 72% [[n1808]], and Cava jumped 26% on same-store sales growth [[n1733]].
Punished

Beats without a raise were not. Microsoft's record earnings beat did not stop a sell-off [[n1492]], Medtronic fell despite a better quarter [[n1488]], and Walmart's market shrugged off a beat [[n1560]] under a cautious outlook [[n1604]]. Software with AI-disruption exposure was marked down hardest: Workday hit a five-year low [[n5465]], C3.ai fell 20.6% [[n1785]], and EPAM Systems fell 20% on a tepid 2026 outlook [[n1573]].
Pattern

Guidance is the pricing unit, not the beat. Three tests separate the winners: the forward outlook (HSBC, Deere, Cava), capital returns, and how exposed the business model is to AI. Salesforce committed $50 billion to buybacks [[n1803]], yet its shares fell on a mixed forecast [[n1836]], so buybacks do not rescue a weak guide. Where AI replaces the revenue, as in software, a beat does not lift the stock; where AI is the supply side, as in Nvidia and memory, the reaction has been smaller than options implied [[n5414]].
Attention into EPS

The previews set up the next tests. CoreWeave is expected to show FY26 upside [[n1825]], but its earnings need to show more for the stock to rise further [[n1835]]. Dell's Q4 preview is about sustaining AI growth [[n1643]], and Stellantis's preview asks whether it is deep value or deep trouble [[n1697]]. These are previews, not results, and the headlines carry no reaction for them. Microsoft shows that previews do not guarantee a reaction: investors dumped its shares despite the largest earnings beat in company history [[n1493]].
Playbook

Own beat-and-raise names into the next print, avoid software stories that rest on a beat alone, and use options on single-name AI-supply stocks because the market already prices the move. Trigger to reverse: a guidance cut from a name whose multiple has been expanding, which would tell the market that the beat was not the point. For the reporting season ahead, size positions on the forecast rather than the print, since the feed shows the stock reaction is decided by the outlook in most cases.

underowned.title: Grid and power capex: the utilities nobody models
parts: Attention Gap

Most attention goes to AI chips and Nvidia, while utilities' multi-year capex plans get less. ConEd plans $38 billion through 2030 [[n1779]], FirstEnergy's five-year plan jumped 30% to $36 billion [[n1617]], and Southern raised its plan to $81 billion as load grows [[n1663]]. Those are rate-base numbers that the consensus models only in outline.
Exposure & Risk

The exposure is regulated utilities and generators: XLU is up 9.05% over 20 sessions and Constellation is up 12.84% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The risk is political. Trump asked Big Tech to bring its own power [[n5553]], and the pledge is short on detail [[n5549]]. Data-centre construction also fell amid permit and power delays [[n5557]]. Moody's flags $662 billion of risk at the heart of the data-centre build-out, concentrated in five companies [[n5457]].
Trigger to Watch

A rebound in data-centre construction, or a signed bring-your-own-power contract with price terms, would turn the grid build-out into consensus. The opposite signal is a pledge that is quietly diluted, which would hit the generators first.

underowned.title: Rare earths and critical minerals: policy, not consensus
parts: Attention Gap

The rare-earth story is treated as a policy story rather than an equity theme. The US took a step in the rare-earth race with China [[n0934]], Japan will subsidise rare-earth recycling to reduce reliance on China [[n0846]], and India and Brazil signed a rare-earths pact [[n0707]]. Zimbabwe's export suspension sent China's lithium price soaring [[n0916]]. Japan is also mining deep-sea mud for rare earths to counter China's chokehold [[n0732]].
Exposure & Risk

Lynas is bigger than Qantas [[n0935]] but missed expectations [[n0936]], so this is a high-beta miner with China-price risk. Instruments are Lynas and rare-earth ETFs, and neither is priced on the card. Governments are hoarding critical minerals [[n0843]], which supports the bid while the policy lasts.
Trigger to Watch
A stockpile tender by the US or Japan would move the theme into consensus. A Chinese price cut that follows a US deal would reverse the premium.

underowned.title: European air defence and drones: the spend is starting
parts: Attention Gap

Defence is discussed as a NATO budget story, but the supply chain is being built now. The UK agreed a drone and missile defence plan with four EU allies [[n3380]], and Europe's main military powers will develop low-cost air-defence systems [[n3383]]. Poland's exit from the anti-personnel mine treaty [[n3382]] shows how fast the policy is moving. Five European nations are launching a joint air-defence and drone programme using Ukrainian expertise [[n3391]].
Exposure & Risk

European defence primes and Polish defence-linked names carry the exposure. The risk is budget timing and the reputational cost of mines. Not every defence name is rising: L3 Harris and other defence stocks took a hit on the day [[n5603]], so the basket is not a single trade.
Trigger to Watch
A joint procurement contract for low-cost air defence would turn the theme into consensus. A delay that pushes the budget into the next fiscal cycle would cool it.

underowned.title: Ultra-long Japanese government bonds: the reflation trade's quiet leg
parts: Attention Gap

Japan's equity rally gets the headlines, with the Nikkei at 58,583.12 and up 10.77% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The long end is where the reflation trade shows. Foreign investors piled into ultra-long JGBs [[n3196]], and Amundi went long Japanese debt for the first time in decades [[n3263]].
Exposure & Risk

Exposure is ultra-long JGB futures and yen forwards. Reflationist board picks have pushed long-term yields up [[n3287]], and the risk is a fiscal sell-off, with the budget debate exposed to scrutiny of gift catalogues [[n3305]]. Japan's fiscal worries are the reason foreign buying has not gone straight to the long end.
Trigger to Watch
A BOJ hike in March or April [[n3274]] would flatten the curve and shift the trade to the front end. A hold with reflationist votes would steepen it, and that is the set-up to own.

crypto.title: Crypto: a bounce that still has to clear $70,000
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin closed at 67,960.12, up 8.39% over 20 sessions and 6.06% in the prior completed daily close (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2026-02-25). Ether closed at 2,054.63, up 12.79% over 20 sessions, and Solana at 87.92, up 12.44%. The rebound follows a bad February: Bitcoin is heading for its worst month since the June 2022 collapse [[n1186]], and spot bitcoin ETFs have logged five straight weeks of outflows [[n1083]]. IBIT closed at 39.23, down 22.52% over 20 sessions, while MSTR closed at 135.65, down 16.05%, and COIN at 183.94, down 12.75% (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2026-02-25). CoinDesk argues that bitcoin's price discovery is moving to Chicago [[n1182]], and a historic mining capitulation is nearing its end, pointing to price stabilisation [[n1257]].
New / Most Important

The constructive headline is stablecoin plumbing. The OCC proposed a framework for regulated stablecoins under the GENIUS Act [[n1280]], and Circle beat revenue expectations with a $770 million fourth quarter as USDC circulation reached $75 billion [[n1292]]; its shares jumped 35% [[n1783]]. Coinbase now offers stock and ETF trading to all US users [[n1238]] and has launched 24-hour equity trading [[n1810]]. Meta is reportedly planning a stablecoin comeback in the second half [[n1195]]. The risk is Sen. Blumenthal's probe of Binance over $1.7 billion in Iran-linked transactions [[n1324]].
Playbook

Mixed. Strategy is Wall Street's most-shorted stock [[n7389]] and rose 8.86% in the prior session, so it is a squeeze risk rather than a clean short. Own spot exposure only if Bitcoin holds the $70,000 hurdle [[n1249]] on a daily close, and buy protection on MSTR and COIN into any squeeze. The trigger to turn bearish is another leg of ETF outflows [[n1204]] with Bitcoin back below its 20-session reference. The bounce is fragile while Jane Street scrutiny of the bitcoin ETF market mechanics continues [[n1269]].

flows.title: Liquidity: rates, dollar and credit point in different directions
parts: Global Liquidity

Global debt reached a record $348 trillion in 2025 as government spending lifted it, the IIF says [[n2559]]. Central banks are not adding much: China has held its lending benchmark for nine months [[n0740]], and India's additional liquidity support is set to wind down after March [[n2575]]. The ECB's leadership is in flux [[n2261]]. Japan's board appointments are a liquidity signal too, with two reflationists picked [[n3239]] that the market read as dovish [[n3272]]. The Bank of England has also increased the hours of CHAPS interbank payments [[n2228]], a small operational sign that liquidity plumbing is being tuned.
Rates & Dollar

The 10Y is 4.05% and the 2Y 3.45% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-25), a bull flattening over 20 sessions with the 10Y 19 bps lower. The DXY at 97.70 is 1.54% higher over 20 sessions, but the dollar fell when the tariffs were struck down [[n2203]] and sellers hit US assets on trade-policy risk [[n2490]]. MarketWatch reports that Trump digging in on tariffs has major implications for the dollar [[n7424]]. TLT closed at 89.91, up 2.40% over 20 sessions, and IEF at 97.34, up 1.42% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), so duration is being bought as the Fed path is read [[n7350]].
Credit Check

Credit is the weak link. LQD closed at 111.65, up 0.76% over 20 sessions, while HYG closed at 80.92, down 0.31% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). Investment grade is holding and high yield is lagging. UBS sees private-credit defaults at 15% in the worst case [[n5152]], and a private-credit fund sold $477 million of assets at 94% of value [[n5148]]. The riskiest CLO funds are flashing a warning [[n2420]], and Nordic bond deals are souring [[n2521]]. Benchmarks for private credit are being built to pierce the opaque market [[n5145]], which is the first step to pricing the risk the card cannot see.
Equity & Fund Flows

Equity flows are rotating rather than fleeing. Global equity funds took their biggest inflow in five weeks as AI concerns eased [[n2372]], but US stocks drew their lowest share of global flows since 2020 [[n2373]]. Hedge funds sold most global equities since April [[n2174]] and are creeping back into tech [[n5129]]. Bitcoin ETF outflows deepened in February [[n1204]], while retail leveraged ETF trading surged [[n4012]]. Buybacks are a distinct flow: Salesforce committed $50 billion [[n1803]], and HSBC's buybacks are on ice until capital recovers [[n0944]]. Hedge funds are offering locked-up private-credit investors a way out, at a hefty discount [[n2477]], which is the clearest sign of stress in the redemption queue.
Portfolio Implication

Mixed. Keep equity beta but hedge credit: stay in investment grade rather than high yield, and buy protection on the high-yield basket. Prefer duration while the curve bull-flattens and the 10Y is 4.05%, and keep a dollar hedge because tariff headlines move the dollar in both directions. The signal to cut risk is LQD's 20-session rise fading or HYG closing below its 80.92 level. The liquidity read is that the rates market is pricing easier policy in 2027 while credit is pricing a slower economy, so the two signals should be sized separately rather than netted off against each other. A portfolio that is long duration and short high yield is the expression of that split, and it is the one the card supports on Feb 25 closes.

anticipatory.title: US tariff step to 15%: refunds and the deficit
parts: What Is Priced

The market treats the 10% global tariff as a bridge rather than an end point. Trump said the tariff could go to 15% 'where appropriate' [[n0931]], and the administration is working to lift it from 10% [[n7313]]. The new levy runs on a 150-day clock [[n3247]], and refunds on the struck-down tariffs could exceed $175 billion [[n7440]]. Pending: the European Parliament is holding the US trade deal on ice [[n2851]].
Conditional Expression

If the tariff goes to 15%, lean into domestic-facing cash flows and utilities, where XLU is up 9.05% over 20 sessions, and trim import-heavy consumer names, where XLY is down 4.56%. If the rate stays at 10% and refunds are paid, the deficit rises and yields reprice higher, so the trade is to reduce duration rather than add it, since the IMF is already calling for US fiscal consolidation [[n6710]].
Risk

The EU says it will accept no increase in US tariffs, 'a deal is a deal' [[n2852]], and Europe is ready to retaliate if the deal is breached [[n2224]]. A tariff step to 15% risks a trade response that European equities, up 4.10% over 20 sessions, would have to absorb.

anticipatory.title: US–China summit in April: yuan strength versus tariff relief
parts: What Is Priced

A steadier US–China track before an April summit [[n0851]] is priced into the yuan, which is near a three-year high [[n0874]], and into Chinese equity proxies that are mixed: ASHR up 2.37% over 20 sessions and KWEB down 10.19%. The countdown to the Trump–Xi meeting is now a headline theme [[n0909]].
Conditional Expression

If the summit delivers tariff relief and chip-export access, the trade is long A-share exposure through ASHR and long the yuan, with the US licence for a small amount of H200 exports as the first sign [[n5428]]. If the summit stalls, the yuan gives back its gains, and the trade is to buy protection on FXI, which is 3.81% lower over 20 sessions at 38.42 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).
Risk

The Japan–China dispute runs in parallel. China has added Japanese entities to its export-control list [[n3249]], so a summit can improve US–China ties while the region still tightens on export controls.

anticipatory.title: March central-bank decisions: BOJ, RBA and BoE
parts: What Is Priced

The market is pricing a hawkish turn outside the US. The BOJ chief flagged a March or April rate-hike chance [[n3274]], a hawkish board member wants more hikes [[n3277]], and the RBA's March meeting is a live question [[n0249]]. The BoE's March cut is an 'open question' for Bailey [[n2229]], while the Fed has its own pause debate [[n7223]].
Conditional Expression

If the BOJ hikes in March, as it has signalled [[n3215]], USD/JPY, at 155.88 on the card, should fall, and the trade is long yen against a dollar that Treasury has been checking [[n3242]]. If the RBA moves in March and the BoE cuts, AUD and GBP split: long AUD/USD on the carry bid [[n0251]] and short GBP/USD at 1.3497 on the cut.
Risk

Reflationist board picks could keep the BOJ on hold while long JGB yields rise [[n3287]]. A hold would move the risk from the yen to the bond market, which is why ultra-long JGBs need their own hedge.

anticipatory.title: Iran talks and OPEC+ in April: oil's risk premium
parts: What Is Priced

Oil carries a risk premium: Brent is up 4.85% over 20 sessions at 70.85, and crude hit seven-month highs on the Iran standoff [[n5117]]. Talks are described as near [[n3006]], and the US has expanded sanctions over oil sales and weapons programmes [[n3009]]. Pending: OPEC+ is to consider a 137,000 bpd increase for April [[n5488]].
Conditional Expression

If talks produce a deal and OPEC+ goes ahead with the increase, the premium deflates: reduce energy, where XLE is up 10.47%, and buy duration. If talks fail and strikes follow, the trade is long oil through USO, at 79.73 and up 5.38% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), with gold as the hedge [[n5637]].
Risk

Russia and Iran are cutting prices to China as oil piles up at sea [[n5487]], so a supply glut can outweigh a geopolitical premium even if talks fail. Political pressure on prices matters too: Forbes reports that Trump falsely claimed gas is below $2.30 in most states [[n5497]], which raises the cost of an oil shock for voters.

catalysts.title: $NVDA — the results reset the AI bar
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Nvidia's fourth-quarter results set the AI bar: record sales of $68 billion [[n5412]], data-centre revenue up 75% and a guidance beat [[n5411]]. The forecast points to accelerating growth as Vera Rubin starts reaching the market [[n5418]], and Nvidia has a licence for a small amount of H200 exports to China [[n5428]]. Thesis: revenue is now driven by shipments rather than sentiment.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The last completed close on the card is 195.56 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), up 3.73% over 20 sessions. Options traders priced the smallest post-earnings swing in three years [[n5414]], so the market is not paying for a repeat surprise. Risk: the US export enforcer says Nvidia has sold zero H200s to China [[n5059]].
Trade Expression

Own shares, or buy a three-month call spread above the card close, sized for a sharp pullback. Invalidation: a quarter in which data-centre growth slows well below the 75% headline, or an export licence that is withdrawn. The 75% data-centre growth headline [[n5411]] is the reference for the bar.

catalysts.title: $ASML — EUV capacity is the next leg
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

ASML's new EUV light source fires three lasers at 100,000 tin droplets a second [[n5069]], with a plan to increase speed by 50% by 2030 [[n5069]]. The 2025 annual report calls AI demand a long-term growth driver [[n5443]], and ASML says China's lithography market is growing at double digits [[n5448]]. The top eight cloud providers' capex is set to exceed $710 billion in 2026 [[n5453]]. Thesis: EUV throughput is a capacity catalyst that sells across the AI chip cycle.
Price Hurdle & Risk

ASML closed at 1,526.51 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), up 4.94% over 20 sessions. The hurdle is a slowdown in the cloud capex cited above, and the risk is that China demand is a cyclical rather than structural lift.
Trade Expression
Buy the shares or the semiconductor ETF SOXX, at 368.00 and up 4.82% over 20 sessions. Invalidation: US export controls tightened on lithography, or a capex cut from the largest cloud providers.

catalysts.title: $MU — memory pricing is still rising
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

The memory cycle is still rising. Samsung lifted prices on its Galaxy S26 amid a chip price surge [[n5477]], and the FT says the memory boom leaves PC and smartphone makers in the cold [[n5475]]. Micron is up 330% in a year [[n5479]]. Thesis: memory pricing is the margin driver, and device-maker pain is evidence of supplier pricing power.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Micron closed at 429.00 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), up 4.57% over 20 sessions. Risk: HP warned the memory crunch will linger into next year and PC sales will slump [[n5109]], which is demand destruction if it spreads to phones.
Trade Expression
Long shares, sized for a sharp drawdown. Invalidation: device-maker orders cut or memory contract prices rolling over, both of which would show up before Micron's guidance does.

catalysts.title: $CEG — the power pledge has a price
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Trump told Big Tech to build its own power plants [[n5553]], and the White House pledge on data-centre power costs [[n5545]] puts the generators in the middle. Constellation closed its Calpine deal [[n4068]] and says power and capacity prices are surging [[n1868]]. Thesis: the power price is real, but the pledge has few details [[n5549]], so the upside is a signed contract rather than a headline.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The card closes CEG at 325.84 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), up 12.84% over 20 sessions and 10.81% over five sessions, which already prices much of the pledge. Risk: NRG says it has zero interest in speculative new capacity [[n1867]], so the build-out may be slower than the headlines.
Trade Expression

Hold the position and do not add above the card close. Use a put spread to protect the gain. Invalidation: a bring-your-own-power contract that carries no price terms, or a pledge that is converted into a rule with no buyers.

catalysts.title: $MSTR — the most-shorted stock is a squeeze risk
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Strategy is now Wall Street's most-shorted stock [[n7389]], and Goldman's list of the most-shorted names includes it alongside Coinbase [[n1314]]. Bitcoin's worst month since 2022 [[n1186]] hits the treasury model. Thesis: the bitcoin premium is gone and short interest is high, so the stock is a squeeze risk rather than a clean short.
Price Hurdle & Risk

MSTR closed at 135.65 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), down 16.05% over 20 sessions but up 8.86% in the prior session. Bitcoin needs to clear the $70,000 hurdle [[n1249]] for the squeeze to become a trend. Risk: a daily close above that level would invalidate the bearish call.
Trade Expression
Bearish through a put spread with an expiry after the next bitcoin catalyst, not a naked short. Invalidation: Bitcoin above $70,000 [[n1249]] on a daily close, or a run of spot-ETF inflows.

catalysts.title: $LLY — pricing pressure from Novo and Washington
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Novo Nordisk cut Wegovy prices in half [[n4063]], and the CMS administrator says most-favoured-nation drug pricing will become the standard [[n5585]]. Trump wants Congress to make his drug pricing deals law, and that will not be easy [[n5582]]. Thesis: price cuts in the obesity class and the MFN push compress the premium for the leader.
Price Hurdle & Risk

LLY closed at 1,028.83 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), 1.03% lower over 20 sessions and 1.28% lower in the prior session. The bear case is about earnings revisions rather than the tape, since the price is already below its level at the start of the window.
Trade Expression
Underweight, or a put spread into the next drug-pricing rule. Invalidation: the MFN push stalls in Congress, or a volume beat offsets the price cuts.

retail.title: Tesla / TSLA — institutions sell, retail buys
parts: Observed Attention

Yahoo Finance reports that as institutional investors sell Tesla, retail investors pile in [[n4006]]. Another 24/7 Wall St. headline says the stock is down 11% in 2026 and Reddit is losing faith fast [[n4030]]. The card has TSLA at 417.40, down 3.13% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The 2026 slide that Reddit is discussing is larger than the 20-session move on the card, so the forum narrative is about the year, not the month.
Motivation & Bias

Retail is buying the dip on a brand story, and the bias is to read institutional selling as a buy signal. Tesla's Europe problem keeps getting worse [[n5156]], which is a fundamental reason to be sceptical of the dip-buying.
Instrument & Risk
Shares or short-dated calls. The risk is that the European sales decline becomes a guidance problem, not a sentiment one.

retail.title: Silver ETF / SLV — the Reddit bears give up
parts: Observed Attention

SLV climbs as Reddit bears wave the white flag [[n4027]], and retail chatter is about silver's recovery above $90 [[n5654]]. A Kitco headline says retail investors remain confident [[n5663]]. The card has SLV at 80.04, up 14.2% over five sessions but down 21.21% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).
Motivation & Bias
Retail is chasing a rebound after a crash, and the bias is recency. The confidence is the sign to be wary of, because the drop was recent enough to still be in memory.
Instrument & Risk

SLV or silver futures. Silver's moves are violent, and one headline ties the drop to China-driven liquidation [[n5665]], so a single exchange flow can reverse the rebound. The 5-session jump of 14.2% sits against a 20-session fall of 21.21%, so the bounce is a retracement, not yet a trend.

retail.title: Opendoor / OPEN — the meme-stock favourite
parts: Observed Attention

Opendoor surged and was called the meme-stock favourite in Barron's [[n3978]]. A 24/7 Wall St. piece says it jumped on an iBuying surge but advises selling [[n6618]]. The card has no Opendoor price, so there is no hurdle to test.
Motivation & Bias
Retail is chasing a housing-rate story. Mortgage rates at the lowest since 2022 [[n6724]] are the bullish argument, and iBuying margin risk is the bearish one, which the retail bias tends to ignore.
Instrument & Risk
Shares only, sized for a gap move. With no card price, any entry needs its own reference point.

retail.title: Oklo / OKLO — the $250 Reddit target
parts: Observed Attention

Oklo is down 24%, but Reddit is betting on a $250 target by July 4 [[n4056]]. The nuclear names are a retail focus, and analysts still see 140% upside in NuScale after its implosion [[n4036]]. The card has no Oklo price.
Motivation & Bias

A price target set on a forum is an anchor, not an analysis, and the bias is to buy the drop. The institutional nuclear trade is elsewhere: Constellation has closed its Calpine deal [[n4068]], while the retail names are chasing targets.
Instrument & Risk
Shares or calls. A single headline can move a stock like this sharply in either direction, so position size matters more than the target.
